uncited: Mesh Voxelization converts a continuous triangular surface mesh (e.g., STL, OBJ) into a discrete 3D voxel grid by determining the occupancy of each grid cell via ray-mesh intersection tests.

Unlike [Rasterization-based Voxelization](908-rasterization-based-voxelization.md), which projects geometry onto a 2D plane and extrudes coverage, this method evaluates the topological relationship (inside/outside) of the voxel center relative to the closed surface using the ray casting parity rule.

It serves as the foundational technique for generating solid or surface-only voxel representations from polygonal models, distinct from [Point Cloud Voxelization](1000-point-cloud-voxelization.md) which operates on discrete samples rather than continuous geometry.

*   **Input:** A triangular mesh defined by vertex positions $V$ and triangle indices $I$; a grid resolution $N$ (or voxel size $s$); a bounding box $[B_{min}, B_{max}]$; and optional parameters for sampling and interior filling.
*   **Output:** A voxel grid $G$ where each cell $(i, j, k)$ contains a boolean occupancy flag, and optionally a Signed Distance Field (SDF) value or attribute data.
**Voxel Grid:** A 3D array of size $N_x \times N_y \times N_z$.
The grid origin is typically aligned with the mesh bounding box.
*   Cast a ray $R(t) = C_{ijk} + t \cdot D$.
*   **Open Mesh Handling:** If the mesh is not watertight, single-direction casting fails.
*   **Open Meshes:** Single-direction ray casting yields incorrect results for non-watertight meshes.
*   **Double-thick Meshes:** Standard odd-even rule fails for double-sided surfaces.
It traverses the volume slice by slice and line by line, maintaining an inside/outside flag that toggles when the scan line spans a voxel intersecting the object boundary.
*   **Time Complexity:** $O(N^3 \cdot T)$, where $N$ is the grid resolution per axis and $T$ is the number of triangles.
*   **Performance:** On an NVIDIA GTX 970, a 64x64x64 voxelization of a 69,664 triangle bunny mesh takes 0.88 seconds with 1 sample, scaling to 51.96 seconds at 256x256x256.
*   **When to use:** When topological correctness (watertightness) is critical and the mesh is closed.
*   **When not to use:** For very high-resolution requirements on complex meshes where rasterization-based methods are faster; for open surfaces where scan-conversion is more appropriate.

Mesh voxelization via ray casting is a fundamental technique in computational geometry and computer graphics, widely used in additive manufacturing (3D printing) preparation, medical imaging, and collision detection.
